ai_summary: Great Britain is currently recording a total wind output of 2.2 GW, with Scottish wind generation contributing an estimated 0.8 GW, representing just 7.9% of installed Scottish wind capacity. While Scotland maintains an exemplary carbon intensity of 0 gCO2/kWh, the GB-wide carbon intensity sits at 154 gCO2/kWh. This regional disparity is driven by grid transmission limits between Scotland and major southern demand centers. So far today, 849 MWh of Scottish generation has been curtailed via the Balancing Mechanism, accumulating a constraint cost of about £47,969. To replace this discarded renewable electricity, fossil plant dispatch resulted in an estimated 161,329 m3 of gas burned elsewhere, emitting an additional 297 tonnes of CO2. Annualizing these figures indicates an estimated total yearly curtailment cost of approximately £18 million. When socialized across the grid through balancing mechanisms, this constraint inefficiency adds an estimated £0.06/MWh to everybody’s invoice in the UK, demonstrating the dual economic and environmental penalty of transmission bottlenecks.
